tone_statements.quote: En cuanto al tono, Silverman nos dice que hay tres: bajo (1), medio (2) y alto (3) y los contornos51 1-2, 3-2, 2-3, 2-1, 3-1 y 1-3-152. Para ejemplificar su teoría, usa la siguiente palabra cuyo significado cambia dependiendo del tono: ʃa3 ‘trabajo’ ʃa2 ‘león de montaña’ ʃa1 ‘molde’ El SLO ha identificado una cuarta palabra: ʃa, ‘alcohol’, que podría representar, o bien un caso de homonimia o bien el cuarto tono —uno más bajo que el representado por el número 3— en la variante de Jalapa de Díaz.
tone_statements.translation: As for tone, Silverman tells us there are three: low (1), mid (2) and high (3), and the contours 1-2, 3-2, 2-3, 2-1, 3-1 and 1-3-1. To illustrate, he uses the following word whose meaning changes with the tone: ʃa3 'work', ʃa2 'mountain lion', ʃa1 'mould'. The SLO [UNAM Otomanguean Languages Seminar] has identified a fourth word, ʃa 'alcohol', which could represent either a case of homonymy or a fourth tone, one lower than that represented by number 3, in the Jalapa de Díaz variety.
tone_statements.locator: p. 31, sec. 1.3 'La variante de San Felipe Jalapa de Díaz' (footnote calls 51, 52 appear inline as '51', '152')
tone_statements.summary: 3 level tones + 6 contours (after Silverman et al.); possible fourth extra-low tone suggested.

tone_statements.quote: En el mazateco, a diferencia del español, cada sílaba se pronuncia con su propio tono, y a veces el tono es la única diferencia entre palabras que se escriben con las mismas letras. Por eso se indica el tono de cada vocal, pues así se especifica el significado de la palabra. El tono alto se representa con un acento escrito sobre la vocal o la n, el tono bajo se representa con una rayita debajo de la vocal o de la n, y el tono medio se reconoce por no tener ni acento ni rayita.
tone_statements.translation: In Mazatec, unlike Spanish, each syllable is pronounced with its own tone, and sometimes tone is the only difference between words written with the same letters. For that reason the tone of each vowel is indicated, since that specifies the meaning of the word. High tone is represented with a written accent over the vowel or the n, low tone with a small line under the vowel or the n, and mid tone is recognised by having neither accent nor line.
tone_statements.locator: p. iii, 'Aclaraciones: Sonidos del mazateco'; glossary notes p. 111 and p. 113
tone_statements.summary: Three tones (high, mid, low) on every syllable, written acute / unmarked / underline in the SIL practical orthography.

sources.note: Text collection whose front matter ('Aclaraciones: Sonidos del mazateco', p. iii) states that every syllable carries its own tone, that tone is sometimes the only difference between words, and that the practical orthography writes three tones: high = acute accent on the vowel or n, low = underline, mid = unmarked (examples ts'ínxá 'trabaja' / ts'i̱nxá 'trabajará' / ts'inxá 'trabajaré'); the glossary introduction (p. 111) says 'El orden alfabético de los tonos es de alto hacia bajo', and the affix list (p. 113) notes for 1sg -a/-á and 2sg -i/-í/-î 'El tono depende del tono final de la raíz'.
